Build makes the package; run starts it. Inspection and logs help you understand what is happening instead of guessing.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Prepare your computer

Install Docker Desktop with Linux containers enabled and the .NET10 SDK. For the full SQL Server stack use supported x64 hardware with enough memory for SQL Server. WPF does not run in the Linux ASP.NET image. Accept applicable vendor licences yourself during installation. Run docker version and docker compose version in a terminal; start Docker Desktop if the engine cannot be reached.

Try the standalone image

docker build -t studylab-api:1 ./Api
docker run --name school-api -d -p 127.0.0.1:5100:8080 studylab-api:1
docker logs school-api
docker inspect school-api
docker stop school-api
docker start school-api
docker rm -f school-api

With no database configuration the standalone image can answer /health, but CRUD needs the database connection supplied by Compose. The health route proves the API process can answer, not that every dependency is healthy. rm removes only this practice container; it does not uninstall Docker.

Registry workflow

docker tag studylab-api:1 YOUR_ACCOUNT/studylab-api:1
docker login
docker push YOUR_ACCOUNT/studylab-api:1
docker pull YOUR_ACCOUNT/studylab-api:1

Use your own registry account and approved access. Do not publish images containing secrets or private student data. Use immutable version tags/digests for reproducible deployment, and scan/update base images. A later pull may differ if a mutable tag was replaced.

Try it yourself

Port5100 is already allocated. What next?

Worked answer

Stop the earlier local API/container or use a different host port, then update the client URL.

What is the difference between stop and rm?

Worked answer

stop ends the process but keeps the container definition/writable layer. rm deletes the container.
